paper_metadata.title: Effect of Nitrogen Doping on the Structure and Mechanical Properties of the Fe40Mn40Cr10Co10 High-Entropy Alloy

evidence.quote: The structure and mechanical properties of as-cast and thermomechanicaly processed (cold rolling followed by annealing at 700 ◦C and 900◦C) Fe40Mn40Cr10Co10 (at.%) high-entropy alloys doped with different amounts (0, 0.5, and 2.0 at.%) of N were examined.

Increasing the annealing temperature to 900 °C resulted in coarsening of the recrystallized grains to 5.6 µm (Figure 4b,d)

The addition of nitrogen resulted in a decrease in the volume fraction of the σ-phase to 5.2% in the N0.5 alloy after annealing at 700 °C (Figure 5a). The σ-phase particles formed continuous films along grain boundaries.
Recrystallization of the fcc phase appeared to be complete. The average grain size was 2.4 µm.

Annealing at a higher temperature of 900 °C resulted in the formation of a homogeneous fully recrystallized single fcc phase structure with the grain size of 6.6 µm (Figure 5b,d). No secondary phases were found.

More detailed investigations by TEM revealed the presence of fine (~70 nm) Cr-rich precipitates (Figure 6c). Most of these precipitates were found in the recrystallized areas; selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns suggested that the particles were hexagonal M2N nitrides.
After annealing at 700 °C, only one half (47%) of the microstructure was recrystallized (Figure 6a). The average size of the recrystallized fcc grains was found to be 1.3 µm.
The increase in the annealing temperature to 900 °C resulted in the formation of a fully recrystallized single fcc phase structure with a grain size of 5.8 µm (Table 3).

The strength of the as-cast alloys at room temperature increased with increasing nitrogen concentration due to interstitial solid solution strengthening.
